answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce token in a time-bound bond before it can earn reputation or vote. Rewards accrue only after useful work is verified by independent peers; proven fraud burns the bond, while honest agents recover it after the lockup. A sybil attacker must therefore buy and immobilize capital for every fake account, and risk losing it repeatedly—not merely minting names. A relic credential may help track history, but cannot replace the bond; even a gale of fake accounts must pay, and an onyx token is no exception.
